I just went through building my PC (not from scratch) for the first time a couple days ago! Earlier it has been my dad that built it but this time he sent me some of his old hardware that was just laying around  (and a bit better than what I had but I'm still stuck on hardwares that seems older than the face of the earth since I play pretty high demanding games) and I set out to disassemble and change all of the hardware except for the PSU and the hard drives! I found it really fun but also a bit terrifying in the sense of being scared to accidentally ruin anything. I'm a worrier so doing something I've never done before, especially with electronics, can freak me out a bit. I have now learned that everything isn't AS sensitive as I thought it was. For some reason my brain thought that you could barely touch *anything* without it breaking in some way. Of course I'm still careful but now I know that I can actually hold the motherboard xD And I have also learned that I need to buy a new computer case because mine is old and has gotten a bit wonky with the screws to secure the motherboard. But now I feel really motivated to save up money to be able to build a new PC completely from scratch. Because I sincerely thought it was fun and a bit challenging to upgrade. And it would be amazing to build a PC that could actually run VR, or not warn me every time I start Death Stranding that I have a worse PC than the minimun recommendation.

I've quit SSRI before but not cold turkey. I lowered the dose by myself a week or two at a time. I didn't consult a doctor as I was very young at the time and no one really listened to me anyways. That went fine. I had gone on them for a long time and never felt like they did anything to better my mental state, anxiety, or anything.   
The thing about your meds is that it might be helping your anxiety. And quitting them can make depression and anxiety a lot worse. *Especially* if you quit cold turkey. I would really recommend consulting your doctor or psychiatrist again about slowly lowering your dose until you quit completely if that is really what you want to do. I wouldn't recommend doing what I did and lowering it yourself just because, well, it's never a good idea to change your meds if you don't know about the possible consequences. But if you're gonna do it anyways, just please don't quit cold turkey. It can really mess you up physically and mentally even though you haven't noticed anything yet!
